status: FULL source Lemmas2.13 and2.14 are proved, including the actual canonical eta identity and constant16 quantitative bound. See periodic-eta-bound-map.json for its exact source correspondence and validation. Full(31),(32)/2.15, Dirichlet C.4(ii) rate and main theorems remain OPEN.
results: A reusable bound is proved over EVERY nontrivially normed scalar field: if norm(P-Q)<=delta and Px=x, then (1-delta)*norm(x)<=norm(Qx). It requires no orthogonality, finite dimension or supplied lower bound.

The LITERAL free projector is CONSTRUCTED independently as a bounded physical operator by the two original Fourier coefficients and exp(+i*pi*n*x), exp(-i*pi*n*x). Its continuous and physical L2 realizations are proved EXACTLY equal to the EXISTING ACTUAL zero-potential source-circle contour projections. This retains the original probability Haar norm, exactly one-half integral on [0,2].

A shared contractive exponent inclusion is constructed on the ENTIRE ORIGINAL Fourier-Lebesgue spaces for EVERY Banach exponent p<=q. Every raw Fourier coefficient and the IDENTICAL ENTIRE original smooth-test distribution are retained. This allows the source eigenfunction domain to be preserved rather than replaced with a supplied native H1 representative.

For EVERY original Fourier-Lebesgue regularity a>3/2 and EVERY Banach exponent p>=1, including p=infinity, a genuine bounded injective inclusion into the ENTIRE ORIGINAL H1 domain is constructed. Its output is the IDENTICAL ENTIRE original distribution. The full source F-ell^(s+2,p) domain with -1/2<s<=0 lies in this range.

Every original native enclosed eigenvector is proved fixed by the ACTUAL physical periodic L2 contour projection. This is derived from the existing native H1/H-minus-one contour theorem and faithful physical inclusions, with no physical spectral range hypothesis supplied.

ONE original endpoint norm-ball cutoff, above ANY supplied previous cutoff and BEFORE EVERY complex potential and ALL later original positive indices, gives the one-half free-mode norm bound on the ENTIRE actual high physical spectral range. Every complex associated-vector direction is included; simple eigenvalues, open gaps and semisimplicity are not assumed.

Every original native high eigenvector in a corrected narrow strip belongs to the SAME literal source-circle physical spectral range. The zero vector is included. For nonzero vectors the proof derives ACTUAL spectral membership, uses the actual high pair to locate the eigenvalue strictly inside the source circle, and applies the ACTUAL native contour action.

The original PRINTED radius-12n source strip is retained in the final native and source Lemma 2.14 statements. The existing full complex wide-strip localization theorem proves that each ACTUAL nonzero eigenvalue in that full wide strip is in the narrow strip at the SAME original mode number. Its stronger 13*C_r cutoff is derived uniformly from the ORIGINAL endpoint norm ball. No radius-6n restriction is substituted for the source statement.

Source Lemma 2.14 is PROVED on the ENTIRE ORIGINAL complex F-ell^(s,infinity) potential space and ENTIRE ORIGINAL F-ell^(s+2,p) eigenfunction space, for EVERY Banach p>=1 including infinity. Its literal full Fourier eigen-equation is PROVED equivalent to the native equation of the IDENTICAL H1 distribution. At EVERY original source eigenvalue in the PRINTED radius-12n strip, the LITERAL free Fourier projector has physical L2 norm at least ONE HALF the norm of the SAME original eigenfunction. ONE cutoff precedes the potential, index, eigenvalue, exponent and eigenfunction and may be chosen above ANY prior spectral cutoff.

Quantitative eta bound 2.13 remains OPEN, although its canonical eta/gamma identity and NOW the required source 2.14 lower bound are proved. Full (31), overlap (32)/2.15, precise Dirichlet C.4(ii) rate, full COMPLEX weighted midpoint 2.1(ii), actual Birkhoff/KdV constructions and ALL FIVE main theorems remain OPEN.

source_correspondence.potential: ENTIRE ORIGINAL complex FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r,infinity), 0<=r<1/2, equivalent to article -1/2<s<=0 by s=-r. The physically period-one complex mean-zero source is included; no reality condition is imposed.
source_correspondence.eigenfunctions: ENTIRE ORIGINAL FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r+2,p), EVERY Banach p>=1 including infinity. The source literal Fourier eigen-equation is retained. A bounded injective inclusion gives an H1 representative with the IDENTICAL ENTIRE original distribution, so its physical L2 realization is the SAME original eigenfunction.
source_correspondence.strip: FULL PRINTED Sn={lambda:abs(Re(lambda)-pi^2*n^2)<=12*n}, represented by wideHillStrip. Existing actual-complex-spectrum localization derives membership in the corrected radius-6n strip at the SAME original n, using a proved uniform stronger cutoff. The final source statement is NOT restricted to the narrow strip.
source_correspondence.free_projector: Literal hillFreeL2ModeProjection n, constructed from F_n*exp(i*pi*n*x)+F_-n*exp(-i*pi*n*x) in the original physical normalization. It is proved EXACTLY equal to the ACTUAL free source-circle contour projector; no free-projection identity is supplied as a hypothesis.
source_correspondence.norm: Original source physical periodic L2 norm, EXACTLY one-half integral on [0,2]. Bound is (1/2)*norm(f)_L2 <=norm(P_n f)_L2; no potential norm or eigenfunction normalization is changed.
source_correspondence.uniformity: For EACH fixed ORIGINAL endpoint norm ball R and ANY prior cutoff Nmin, ONE new N>=2 and N>=Nmin is chosen BEFORE every original complex potential q, all later original positive n, every complex lambda in the FULL printed strip, EVERY Banach p and EVERY original eigenfunction. This is stronger than the source locally uniform cutoff requirement.
source_correspondence.stronger_range_bound: The SAME one-half bound holds on the ENTIRE actual high physical spectral range, including complex associated vectors and coincident spectral roots. It does not require a nonzero or normalized eigenfunction premise.
